criteria.title: System discovery advertises the LLM control-plane contract only when LLM is enabled
criteria.assertion: `/api/v1/system/info` must advertise `llm_routes`, `llm_deployments`, and `llm_rollback` capabilities plus the LLM request kinds `5971-5975`, status kind `6973`, result kinds `7971-7973`, and read-model kinds `31964-31965` only when the LLM feature is enabled, and must omit those LLM-specific entries when the feature is disabled.
preconditions: System info handler is exercised once with `llmEnabled=true` and once with `llmEnabled=false`.
steps: Request or construct the control-plane info payload in both enabled and disabled configurations.
Inspect capabilities, request kinds, status kinds, result kinds, read-model kinds, correlation tags, and MCP fields.
criteria.expected_result: The enabled payload contains the full LLM contract surface; the disabled payload does not advertise it.
negative_cases: If the disabled payload still advertises LLM control-plane kinds or capabilities, the criterion fails.
If the enabled payload omits any of the canonical LLM kinds or route/release correlation fields, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: LLM route creation uses a signer-first correlated request/result contract
criteria.assertion: Creating an LLM route must publish a signed kind `5971` request, require at least one accepted relay publish, and produce a correlated kind `7971` terminal result carrying `route_id`, `status=success`, and reply tags linking the result to the originating requester and request event.
preconditions: A signer-capable caller can publish canonical LLM request events.
At least one control-plane relay is reachable for the success case.
steps: Publish an LLM route create request with valid route payload.
Observe publish acceptance and the correlated terminal result event.
criteria.expected_result: The request is signed, at least one relay accepts it, and a correlated `7971` result resolves the operation with the created `route_id`.
negative_cases: If zero relays accept the request and the caller is still told the route was created, the criterion fails.
If the terminal result lacks correlation to the originating request or requester, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: LLM release registration uses a signer-first correlated request/result contract
criteria.assertion: Registering an LLM release must publish a signed kind `5972` request scoped to a route, require at least one accepted relay publish, and produce a correlated kind `7972` terminal result carrying `route_id`, `release_id`, and `status=success`.
preconditions: A signer-capable caller can publish canonical LLM request events.
steps: Publish an LLM release registration request containing route and release payload fields.
Observe publish acceptance and the correlated terminal result event.
criteria.expected_result: The request is signed, at least one relay accepts it, and a correlated `7972` result resolves the operation with the created `release_id`.
negative_cases: If the release request is accepted without route correlation, the criterion fails.
If the terminal result omits `release_id` or fails to correlate to the originating requester and request event, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: LLM deploy requests are signer-first, explicitly tagged, and accepted asynchronously
criteria.assertion: Deploying an LLM release must publish a signed kind `5973` request carrying explicit `route`, `environment`, and `release` correlation tags, fail pre-acceptance when no relay accepts the request, and on acceptance return a correlated kind `6973` reply whose semantic meaning is `accepted for async processing`, not terminal success.
preconditions: A route, release, and environment are available.
A signer-capable caller can publish canonical LLM request events.
steps: Publish a valid deploy request.
Observe relay acceptance behavior and the first correlated reply event.
criteria.expected_result: The request is signed and explicitly tagged, zero-accept publish fails locally, and successful acceptance yields a correlated `6973` reply with `status=processing` and step `accepted`.
negative_cases: If the caller treats the initial accepted status as a completed deployment, the criterion fails.
If a deploy request can succeed without explicit route/environment/release correlation tags, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: LLM deployment approval and rejection remain signer-first and stateful
criteria.assertion: Approving or rejecting a protected-environment LLM deployment intent must use a signed kind `5974` request correlated by `intent` and `decision`, reject invalid decisions before mutation, publish a correlated kind `7973` terminal result, and on rejection repair the desired route state away from the rejected intent.
preconditions: A pending protected-environment LLM deployment intent exists.
steps: Publish an approval request for a pending intent.
Publish a rejection request for a pending intent in a separate run.
Inspect the resulting terminal replies and route-state mutation.
criteria.expected_result: Valid decisions mutate intent state and publish correlated terminal `7973` replies; rejection removes the rejected intent from desired route-state selection; invalid decisions fail with validation error and no mutation.
negative_cases: If a decision other than `approve` or `reject` mutates deployment state, the criterion fails.
If rejected intents remain the desired route state after rejection repair should have run, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Accepted LLM deployments emit progress and terminal outcomes through the async provisioning path
criteria.assertion: After an LLM deploy request has been accepted, the asynchronous provisioning path must emit correlated `6973` progress replies for meaningful deployment stages and eventually publish a terminal `7973` result with completed or error status; failures must complete the run as failed and must not be reported as successful deployment completion.
preconditions: An accepted LLM deployment intent exists and the provisioning coordinator is active.
steps: Run a successful LLM deployment from accepted intent through completion.
Run a failing LLM deployment that hits provisioning, gate, or gateway-sync failure.
criteria.expected_result: Successful runs emit progress then terminal completion; failing runs emit progress up to failure and a terminal error result, with run/state records reflecting failure instead of success.
negative_cases: If a failed run emits a success terminal result, the criterion fails.
If accepted deployments never emit a terminal `7973` outcome, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Authoritative LLM route and route-state projections are published and reconciled
criteria.assertion: Bahia must publish replaceable `31964` LLM route registry projections and `31965` LLM route-state projections from authoritative state, and the route-state projection must reflect desired release/intent plus observed backend and gateway status after observation/reconcile updates.
preconditions: Authoritative route, release, intent, run, or observation state exists.
steps: Republish or update LLM route and route-state projections from authoritative state.
Record an observation or run reconcile against backend and gateway state.
criteria.expected_result: `31964` and `31965` projections are published, and route-state content tracks desired-vs-observed backend/gateway state including drift and gateway status changes.
negative_cases: If LLM route-state changes are not projected after authoritative state changes, the criterion fails.
If reconcile observations cannot influence projected backend/gateway state, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Browser-visible LLM control-plane state comes from Bahia-authored relay events
criteria.assertion: The shared browser control-plane store must populate `llmRoutes`, `llmRouteStates`, and LLM deployment activity from Bahia-authored relay events, ignore spoofed authors, and keep the collections reactive to live `31964`, `31965`, `6973`, and `797x` events after bootstrap.
preconditions: The browser has bootstrapped the shared control-plane store with an advertised Bahia service pubkey.
steps: Bootstrap the shared control-plane store.
Deliver valid LLM route/state/status/result events from the Bahia service pubkey.
Deliver spoofed events from a non-Bahia author.
criteria.expected_result: Valid Bahia-authored events update LLM route/state/activity collections; spoofed authors are ignored; live updates remain reactive after bootstrap.
negative_cases: If spoofed non-Bahia events populate LLM route or state collections, the criterion fails.
If live LLM events stop updating browser-visible state after bootstrap, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Approved product contract requires a dedicated end-user browser workflow and excludes legacy operational REST mutations
criteria.assertion: The approved product contract for this slice requires a dedicated browser-visible workflow that lets an end user create an LLM route, register a release, initiate deployment, review approval state, and observe resulting route-state/activity using signer-first Nostr requests plus relay-backed read models; that workflow must not depend on the deprecated operational REST mutation endpoints `/api/v1/llm/intents`, `/approve`, `/reject`, `/rollback`, `/hosts`, or `/observations` as normative behavior.
preconditions: The LLM control-plane feature is enabled for the browser-facing product surface.
steps: Exercise the browser-visible LLM workflow from route/release creation through deploy and approval visibility.
Inspect the transport and route dependencies used by that workflow.
criteria.expected_result: The workflow is present and user-visible, uses signer-first LLM request kinds plus relay-backed read models, and does not require the deprecated operational REST mutation surface as part of the approved contract.
negative_cases: If the product exposes only passive shared-store visibility with no dedicated user workflow, the criterion fails.
If the approved browser workflow relies on `/api/v1/llm/intents`, `/approve`, `/reject`, `/rollback`, `/hosts`, or `/observations` as normative mutations, the criterion fails.

coverage_notes: This approved AC set covers the non-rollback portion of the LLM control-plane slice because rollback semantics were explicitly deferred by HITL-LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT-004.

Several criteria are grounded in current backend, projection, and shared-store evidence, while the dedicated end-user browser workflow criterion is authorized by prior HITL and is expected to fail until that workflow is implemented.
Observed operational REST mutation routes remain useful legacy evidence, but they are not part of the approved intended contract for future test generation.
unresolved_questions: What explicit rollback target-selection and supersedence rule should replace the current implementation before rollback-specific acceptance criteria and tests are generated?
